wrappedAsset: Fungible Asset (0x1::fungible_asset) minted by the bridge module -- no separate deployed address, it's a resource of the package itself

realDryRun.notes: Real BSC -> Aptos Testnet transfer through a brand-new native Move contract (aptos/programs/inaya-bridge-aptos), NOT Wormhole -- built after Wormhole's own SDK proved genuinely blocked for both Aptos and Sui (stale, hardcoded per-asset bytecode templates the SDK ships, confirmed by re-running the actual attestation attempt live and inspecting the exact bytecode/package-version mismatch -- see deployments/interop/wormhole-wtt/bscTestnet-attestation.json's SUI/APTOS entries). Design choice worth recording: unlike Solana (whose native secp256k1 precompile keccak-hashes the message internally, an undocumented quirk requiring a special double-hash on the signer side), Aptos's aptos_std::secp256k1::ecdsa_recover applies NO hidden hashing -- so this contract reuses the exact same EIP-191 personal-sign convention every EVM spoke's validator signing code already produces (ethers.Wallet.signMessage), no special-cased signing logic needed. Worked end-to-end on the first real attempt -- no crypto/hashing bugs found, only shell/CLI tooling friction (documented in scripts/relayer-dry-run-aptos.mjs).
